scope: Local backend, structured-memory helper and PostgreSQL-compatible persistence regressions. No model calls, remote data writes, public Auth claims or browser operations.
changes: Global memory OFF and ON use matching forward-only extraction and summary consent floors.
Related-person consent and alias changes invalidate in-flight revision snapshots and old derived summaries.
Related-person withdrawal or deletion leaves a content-free suppression even when no structured memory existed.
Initial related-person registration invalidates old derived context without blocking later future opt-in.
Extraction and summary receive current allowed and blocked related-person lists; blocked known-alias turns and assistant echoes are excluded before model requests.
Structured output that reintroduces a blocked known alias is rejected or omitted.
Reply context excludes current known blocked aliases even from pre-existing USER-attributed memories, without deleting those rows or ordinary raw conversation.
The privacy RPC supplies the complete aggregated blocked-person list; missing or failed privacy metadata fails closed.
Account cascade does not recreate a tombstone after the Auth owner is gone.

Before a non-consenting alias leaves the blocked set through deletion, rename or opt-in, exact normalized alias matches in derived memory rows are retired; unrelated USER rows and original messages remain. NFKC and case normalization are tested.
deploymentOrder: Apply migration 202609190013_memory_consent_boundaries.sql before deploying the changed Edge context reader.
limitations: Alias exclusion is conservative matching of known registered non-consenting people, not a claim of recognizing all unknown people or implicit references.
Any durable forgetting suppression conservatively prevents summary reconstruction; retiring an alias-matched USER row also creates that row's ordinary scope/subject suppression.
The bounded real-provider maintenance suite remains pending migration deployment and stable-provider selection.
